name: Google Cloud Bigtable
tagline: Google's managed wide-column store, the original Bigtable, with HBase API and SQL access.
description: Cloud Bigtable is the externally offered version of the system that has backed Google Search, Maps and Gmail since the mid-2000s. You get a sorted, sparse, petabyte-scale table keyed by a single row key, with throughput that scales linearly by adding nodes and replication across clusters in multiple regions. It speaks the HBase client API and, since 2025, GoogleSQL for reads, and change streams feed Dataflow and BigQuery. It is excellent for time-series, ad-tech and ML feature serving where row-key design is everything, and a poor fit for small or relational datasets because of its per-node minimum cost.

pricing.notes: Billed per node-hour (or autoscaled compute), plus SSD/HDD storage and network; committed-use discounts available.

scale.notes: Storage separated from compute on Colossus; multi-cluster routing accepts writes in any replicated cluster with eventual consistency between them.

strengths: Linear throughput scaling by adding nodes, with consistent low-millisecond latency
HBase API compatibility eases Hadoop migrations
Multi-region replication with automatic failover routing
Change streams and native BigQuery, Dataflow and Spark integration
No storage limit per table; storage and compute scale independently
weaknesses: Single row key index; no secondary indexes
Single-row atomicity only, no multi-row transactions
Minimum node cost makes small workloads expensive
GCP-only; hot-spotting from poor row-key design hurts badly
useCases: Ad-tech user profiles and bidding data
HBase workloads moving to the cloud
